rich_summary: Arjuna, still disguised as a Brahmana after winning Draupadi at her swayamvara, confronts Karna on the battlefield. Karna, sensing extraordinary skill, wonders if his opponent is a god or legendary warrior. Arjuna maintains the Brahmana disguise but declares he has mastered divine weapons and intends to defeat Karna. Respecting the supposed Brahmanical power, Karna withdraws. Elsewhere Bhima wrestles the mighty Salya and dramatically throws him down, astonishing the gathered kings, who begin to suspect the mysterious Brahmanas are no ordinary men. Krishna also perceives the truth—that they are the sons of Kunti—and persuades the monarchs to cease fighting. The Pandavas return to their humble dwelling and present Draupadi to their mother as “alms.” Without seeing her, Kunti tells them to share what they have brought, inadvertently creating the dilemma that leads to Draupadi’s unique marriage to the brothers.

highlight_spans.why: Karna questions the identity of his mysterious opponent, hinting that only divine or legendary warriors could fight him.
Bhima and Salya’s brutal wrestling match showcases Bhima’s physical dominance and the Pandavas’ hidden prowess.
The assembled kings realize the supposed Brahmanas must be extraordinary warriors, foreshadowing the Pandavas’ revealed identity.
Kunti’s unintended command to 'enjoy all what ye have obtained' creates the pivotal moral and narrative dilemma leading to Draupadi’s shared marriage.

top_scenes.scene_text: Bhima lifts the powerful king Salya in his arms during their wrestling duel and hurls him across the arena while stunned monarchs watch.
Arjuna, disguised as a humble Brahmana, stands calmly with his bow facing the suspicious Karna amid a tense battlefield crowd.
Inside the potter’s humble hut, Kunti unknowingly tells her sons to share their 'alms' as Draupadi stands beside them, the brothers realizing the gravity of her words.
